intents.title: The system steers itself, instead of only executing well
intents.why:
Measured 2026-09-01 across the working tree, populations stated in the design series: the system built EXECUTION and INTEGRITY to a high standard and never built the STEERING. Of 24 declared functions, 5 work, 14 are partial and 5 are missing outright — and all five missing ones are steering (priority propagation, WIP control, constraint diagnosis, capability build as a governed function, capability retirement). The consequences are measurable rather than felt: backlog net +425 rows in August against +37 in May; 196 dated sprint logs of which 1.0% deployed to real money, deployment being the only category that FELL while throughput tripled; 256 of 370 research units superseded before anyone read them; 1 of 117 dispositions producing an action; 6 strategy retirements ever, none in five weeks; 21 of 32 milestones simultaneously active.
The root cause is not rigour, effort or tooling — all three are unusually strong. It is that one undifferentiated session type does three incompatible jobs, guided by a ~403,000-token map no session can hold, with four competing "what next" surfaces and no arbiter, and no forcing function that removes anything.
intents.doneLooksLike: The operator's cycle decision has a computed constraint behind it; work in flight is capped and visible; a session inherits its context from the work rather than from the corpus; and something has actually been retired. NOT "all 8 phases merged" — a phase that merged and changed nobody's behaviour has not delivered this intent.

extra.⚠️_this_intent_is_capability_work: E2 capability build is supposed to be PULLED by a held-up stage, never self-started. This is pulled by an operator directive instead, because E1 (constraint diagnosis) does not exist yet to give a diagnosis. That is a legitimate source — A2 priority is operator-set by design — but it is a DIFFERENT one, and recording it as a constraint finding would be the unprovenanced conclusion this repo keeps paying for. The measured constraint is DECISION, and only phase F acts on it directly.

objects.title: Phase F — the repairs — decision preparation and decision recording
objects.reviewTrigger: Re-read when the phase it depends on closes, or when the operator changes the cycle priority. A dormant phase is not a queued one — it is re-argued when it becomes reachable.
objects.doneCondition: A strategy-review packet is committed on a cadence and read, and a Tier-3 approval lands in exactly one place.
objects.note: ⚠️ THIS IS THE ONLY PHASE THAT IS UNBLOCKED TODAY, and it is the only one that touches the MEASURED constraint (DECISION). It depends on nothing this build produces. strategy_review_packet.py is 1,518 lines that emit a real action badge with reasons and an SLA, and write to a GITIGNORED path with no cron — so no packet has ever been committed. The repair is a cron and a committed path. C4: strategy_changelog.json has been dead since 2026-07-28, and squeeze_breakout_4h runs live today against a written record saying it was demoted for a 0% win rate over 60 closes.

scope_split.c3_decision_preparation: IN FLIGHT 2026-09-01. The cron (.github/workflows/strategy-review-packets.yml), --all-strategies, write_index(), and the committed path comms/strategy_reviews/. ⚠️ NOT done until a dispatched run has actually COMMITTED an INDEX.json — a green run with no committed index is a failure, not a pass.
scope_split.c4_decision_recording: DEFERRED, with a stated reason rather than silently dropped. C4 wants one decision record instead of four forked surfaces, and the obvious first move — a guard comparing the changelog's execution verdict against config/strategies.yaml — CANNOT be built honestly today: the 53 changelog entries carry only {date, ref, summary}, so the verdict exists solely as PROSE ("DEMOTED execution: live -> shadow ..."). Extracting it by pattern-matching English is sub-class A of the diagnostic-provenance defect this repo has a guard family for, and a guard that matches prose would be confidently wrong on the entries it misses. The honest path is a STRUCTURED field on new entries plus a reported denominator of un-structured ones — which is a design decision, not a wire, and belongs to its own change.
scope_split.⚠️_do_not_read_this_object_as_c4_deliver: A concrete live instance is already filed as BL-20260901-DECISION-RECORD-SAYS-SHADOW-WHILE-CONFIG-SAYS-LIVE-SQUEEZE-BREAKOUT-4H, whose resolution_criteria require BOTH a reconciliation AND the executable check — because closing the instance without the check is exactly what left this class alive the two previous times it was fixed.

It is deliberately NOT `done`: its done_condition is an OBSERVATION nobody has made yet, and the channel it rides is itself unproven (OI-20260826). `waiting` is the honest state — a `done` here would be the collapse the six-state vocabulary exists to prevent, and would quietly convert "we deployed it" into "we verified it".

So this object's done-condition is an OBSERVATION, not a deploy.

blockedOn.note: The pull rule requires E1 to be able to NAME the held-up stage a capability claims to unblock; without it the rule is unenforceable.

objects.note: 6 strategy retirements have ever occurred, none in five weeks against 45 live legs, and nothing has ever retired a skill, register, workflow or guard. Complexity is monotonic by construction until something removes. ⚠️ A retirement is done when the old thing is GONE, not when the replacement ships.

blockedOn.note: The control half extends the read view; building both at once would couple the cheap half to the gated one.
Gating reads is only tractable once there is nothing else left to keep working.
A route gate is authentication, not authorization: one token would otherwise open all 22 tables.

objects.note: require_session is genuinely default-deny and already tested; exactly two routes attach it today. /api/auth/login was built for this and NO consumer has ever called it. ⚠️ A static site cannot hold a secret — the SPA is served from GitHub Pages, so the operator logs in and the browser holds a short-lived session token.

wip.note: The ceiling of 8 is DECLARED but not enforced. Enforcement ships in Phase C together with the backlog migration, because a ceiling with no real rows behind it is meaningless and the rows without a ceiling are the condition the redesign exists to end. This count is a reading, not a gate.

coverage.note: This store holds the operating-layer build's own phases and nothing else. The carried backlog rows (~572 not-closed) migrate in Phase C, together with the WIP ceiling. A bug to fix still goes to the review backlogs; what a session must KNOW before it plans is still OPEN-ITEMS.json. Do not read this as the whole of the system's work.
